title: Log filename launcher-pid spec: make pid= the shell-invoked launcher, and revive the dead rotation it gates
desc: DESIGN SPEC, not yet implemented. Why the pid in a wkappbot-core.exe.out-* log filename should be the shell-invoked LAUNCHER pid instead of the writing core pid, why that also unblocks RotateOldLogs which has had zero call sites since 2026-05-07, the two transports needed because an ancestry walk is wrong on the Eye-pipe path, the ElevationHelper trap that forbids touching eye.pid logs, and the verification that proves it by what moves.
steps: PROBLEM. A command log filename answers which process WROTE it and cannot answer which shell command CAUSED it. Every pid= in a log name is Environment.ProcessId of the writing core or Eye process (EyeCmdPipeServer.Dispatch.cs:32,105,184; AppBotEyeCommands.cs:571,659,1410; AppBotEyeGlobalMode.cs:230). The launcher writes NO log file at all -- its pid survives only in stderr prose and a volatile TEMP relay file. AppendLauncherErrorRecord (CoreRunner.Part2.cs) is the launcher's ONLY persistent record and it carries NO pid field, though its log field points forward at the core log. So launcher-to-core is traceable and core-to-launcher is not.

THIS IS NOT COSMETIC, IT UNBLOCKS A DEAD GARBAGE COLLECTOR. RotateOldLogs (AppBotProgramInfra.cs:188) moves a stale out-log into old_cmdTag only after TryGetPidFromLogName reads the pid and IsProcessAlive says the writer is gone. TWO defects stack. FIRST, the function has ZERO call sites: 2026-05-06 had two files containing the call, 2026-05-08 had one, today still one. The caller was dropped by fa4a0f911b, refactor(program) split Program.cs for the 400-line cap, whose own message reads Build clean 0 warnings 0 errors -- a dead function compiles perfectly. SECOND, even restored it would move nothing: under Eye-pipe delegation the writing core IS the long-lived Eye daemon, so measured 2026-09-03 an out-log named pid=10788 sat beside a live eye.diag.pid=10788 and IsProcessAlive answers true for essentially every command log forever. A launcher pid dies when the command ends, which is what finally makes that gate mean this command is finished.

FORMAT, keep the shape and change the value: wkappbot-core.exe.out-{ts}.{cmdTag}.pid={launcherPid}.log. No new segment and no reordering, so TryGetPidFromLogName (:243), OldSubDirFromCmdTag (:223), the out-log rotation glob (:194) and the FileWatchers glob (FileWatchers.cs:306) are all untouched. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE and why: appending .lpid={launcherPid} AFTER .pid= parses safely, since the literal .pid= needs a dot then p while .lpid= has a dot then l so they never collide, but it leaves the rotation gate still reading a daemon pid and therefore buys readability while fixing nothing. NEVER place a new segment BEFORE .pid=: OldSubDirFromCmdTag slices everything between the timestamp and .pid= as the command tag AND USES THAT AS THE FOLDER NAME, so the tag would become skill-read.lpid=1234 and rotation would create one folder per launcher pid.

SCOPE is command logs only, and the daemon self-logs must NOT change. eye.pid=NNN.log and eye.diag.pid=NNN.log are a daemon's own log where the pid IS the subject and no per-command launcher exists. THE TRAP: ElevationHelper.Launch.cs:65-84 sweeps any eye.pid log whose pid is dead or non-core into _crashed/, so putting a launcher pid there classifies every daemon log an orphan on sight -- a silent mass-misfiling, not a crash. Restrict the change to the wkappbot-core.exe.out-* family.

TWO TRANSPORTS, because an ancestry walk is right for one path and silently WRONG for the other. PATH A, launcher spawns the core directly via CoreRunner: the core is the launcher's child, so pass Environment.ProcessId as a spawn ARGUMENT rather than an environment variable -- this repo already treats an identity-bearing env var as a spoof vector (the WKHARNESS_AGENT_MODEL block) and an argument is visible in the command line where a reviewer can see it. PATH B, delegation over the Eye pipe: the Eye is NOT a descendant of this launcher, it was started by an earlier one, so an ancestry walk returns a different and usually dead launcher -- a wrong answer indistinguishable from a right one. Send __lpid:{launcherPid} over the existing internal-argument channel; __hwnd, __hwnd_rect and __hwnd_dpi already travel that way (EyeCmdPipeServer.Pipe.cs:135-206) and Dispatch.cs:265 already excludes every __ prefixed argument from help lookup. PATH C, core started by the Eye with no launcher: keep the core's own pid, never invent one and never write pid=0.

DO NOT BUILD ON IsLauncherInParentChain(). The skill core-worker-logging-launcher-chain-ref step 2 presents it as the v5.13.133 mechanism, but a case-insensitive grep for IsLauncher or LauncherInParent across csharp/src returns ZERO hits -- the name is not in the tree. That skill drift needs correcting separately and nothing here may rest on it.

WHICH LAUNCHER: pin the ORIGINAL. HelpAndAliases.cs:39-54 re-execs the launcher when it finds itself stale, printing SWAP pid= then SWAP new-pid= and waiting, so after a swap the launcher the shell started and the launcher that reaches the core are different processes. The owner asked for the pid THE SHELL KNOWS, so the first launcher stamps its own and every later hop FORWARDS the value it received; only a launcher that received nothing uses Environment.ProcessId.

TWO THINGS THE FORMAT CHANGE CANNOT DO ALONE. (1) Restore the caller or this spec is inert -- re-wire RotateOldLogs into the path that lost it, honouring CoreRunner.Part3.cs:12 which records a 26-second hang on a slow drive, so run it off the critical path and bounded. (2) Add a pid-independent AGE FLOOR: a Path-C log still carries a live daemon pid and would never rotate, and the entire back-catalogue predating this change carries daemon pids too. Also confirm liveness by pid AND image name, because Windows reuses pids and a recycled launcher pid landing on an unrelated live process pins its log at top level forever.

VERIFY BY WHAT MOVES AND WHAT REFUSES TO MOVE, never by reading the diff, because nothing here crashes when it is wrong -- it silently records the wrong identity, stops rotating, or mass-misfiles daemon logs as crashes. (1) Run one command through the direct path and one through the Eye pipe: both filenames carry the launcher pid visible in the shell and the two differ. (2) THE REGRESSION THAT PROVES THE POINT: run a command, let it finish, wait past the stale window, run rotation, and assert the file MOVED into old_cmdTag -- today it never does. (3) Eye-internal core with no launcher: filename unchanged and the age floor still retires it. (4) Daemon logs still carry the daemon pid and ElevationHelper moves NOTHING new into _crashed -- count that folder before and after. (5) Force a SWAP and assert the FIRST launcher's pid. (6) Join test: read a failing command's errors.jsonl record and reach its log by pid alone.

SECOND HALF, close the return edge. AppendLauncherErrorRecord currently emits ts, exit, source, cmd, log and fields with no pid at all. Add a pid field carrying the launcher pid, append-only so every existing reader keeps working, and the join then closes both ways: the errors.jsonl pid matches the pid= in the filename, same number and same meaning. RELATED WORK THAT BELONGS WITH THIS: cmdTag itself embeds command ARGUMENTS today, which is why 1240 old_ folders accumulated with names such as old_speak_ followed by a whole Korean sentence, so sanitising cmdTag ships alongside.

LANDED 2026-09-03, the GC HALF of this spec, in GcCommand.cs. TWO defects fixed. OVER-SCOPE: roots was DataDir plus Directory.GetDirectories, so a bare run walked EVERY wkappbot.hq subfolder and any folder missing from the retentionDays map took the 30-day default -- that is how gc --days 7 --sweep recycled eight tracked config files, two of them live auth cookies. Now a purgeable HashSet built from retentionDays.Keys gates a bare run, an explicitly NAMED folder is still honoured because naming one is deliberate, all means every purgeable folder rather than every folder, and loose files in the HQ root require an explicit all instead of being swept by default. Every refusal prints a line, so the behaviour is visible rather than silent. THE HANG: the pre-scan ran Directory.GetFiles AllDirectories plus a FileInfo per file for EVERY subfolder BEFORE any filtering; it now runs only for a folder that will actually be touched and is bounded by a 1000-file cap that prints 1000+ rather than enumerating further. VERIFIED BY WHAT IT REFUSES, live dry-run against a real HQ: chrome-profiles, profiles, runtime and skills all printed SKIPPED while logs was the only folder processed -- build 0 errors, 14 pre-existing warnings. STILL OWED and deliberately not attempted here: the pid= value itself is unchanged, so the rotation gate still reads a daemon pid, and RotateOldLogs still has zero call sites. A wired proto for the caller exists at .tmp/Program.Dispatch-rotatelogs-wired-proto.cs but its fixture test was never run, so treat it as unproven.

NAVIGATION: this core carries the DESIGN -- the filename format, the two transports, the scope limit and the verification. WHEN: you are about to implement or review the pid change, or you hit a claim here you want the evidence for. HOW: run wkappbot skill read log-filename-launcher-pid-spec-ref for the dated measurements (the revision bisect that dated the dead caller, the daemon-pid collision, the eight tracked files a gc sweep destroyed) and for the three approaches ALREADY RULED OUT so you do not re-derive them; run wkappbot skill read repo-garbage-collector-unused-file-quarantine for the quarantine-not-delete policy this work sits inside. WHY: the measurements and the incident history are what make the design arguments checkable rather than assertions, and separating them keeps this core readable at the size where a reader actually reads it.

INCIDENT: the dead RotateOldLogs caller and the never-assigned ActiveTee are ONE regression, not two -- commit de22fc5ba5 on 2026-05-07 dropped both, and the direct-core path has written no per-command log since. WHEN: you are implementing this spec, or you cannot find a command's output in any log, or two separate investigations here each report a 2026-05-07 date and you are treating them as coincidence. HOW: grep the ASSIGNMENT, never the declaration -- run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto first, then 'grep -rn "ActiveTee = " csharp/src' returns NOTHING while Program.cs:20 declares the field, and 'git show de22fc5ba5^:csharp/src/WKAppBot.CLI/Program.cs' still holds the original block: OriginalStdout, the RunningInEye-guarded TeeTextWriter construction, ActiveTee = tee, the ThreadRoutingWriter install and the [LOG] line. WHY: measured 2026-09-04. That commit was a mechanical 400-line-cap split; it deleted the block that CREATES the tee and kept every reader of it, so Program.Dispatch.cs:201-204 sets ExitCode, writes the error record, restores the console and disposes -- all against a permanently null field -- and McpCommand.ErrorBuffer.cs:27 reads the same null. Then 54f0529a95, the SAME DAY, changed the field to '= null' to clear CS0649, whose text is literally 'never assigned'; the one instrument that reported the regression was switched off before anyone read it. It hid for four months because the Eye path builds its own tee at EyeCmdPipeServer.Dispatch.cs:34, so logs kept appearing. That matters right now: the launcher is currently falling back from the Eye pipe to Core on ordinary commands, so those runs pass through with no log and no error record at all -- which is why this spec's own verification step 1, comparing a direct run against an Eye run, cannot be performed until the block is restored.
